WEEK MODULE MAP (ungraded orientation)

Mass Culture and Culture War in the 1920s

THIS WEEK

This week looks at two faces of the 1920s: a new shared culture of radio, movies, and jazz, and the sharp quarrels over drink, race, religion, and who counts as a real American.

Take the pages in this order: the lesson "Radio, Movies, and a Shared Culture," then the source W. E. B. Du Bois, "Of Mr. Booker T. Washington and Others", then the lesson "Prohibition, the Klan, Scopes, and Garvey," and then the source Marcus Garvey, Philosophy and Opinions. Read each lesson before the source that follows it, since the lessons give you the background you need to read the sources well.

What to turn in: this week's main assignment is a VR Activity, which you complete in your VR headset. You will also take part in the discussion "Jazz Age or Culture War: Which Was the Real 1920s?" Instructions, due dates, and links for both are in Canvas.

When you finish, open the Week Wrap-Up page and use its checklist to confirm that everything is submitted.
